paragraphs: Telford & Wrekin Council runs its own fostering service, Telford Fostering, and the services shown above also cover the borough. The council's case is that fostering locally keeps children near the people and places they know, and in May 2024 it said Telford and Wrekin needed many more fostering households.

Figures the fostering service gave councillors in April 2024, reported by the Shropshire Star, show where the gaps are. There were 173 approved fostering households in the borough with 183 children living with them, and 20 vacancies the council was still trying to fill. Between April 2022 and March 2023 it received 25 applications and approved 15 households. Of the 37 teenagers who came into care after April 2023, 21 went to the council's own carers, nine to external foster carers and seven to residential homes, so people willing to care for teenagers are especially worth hearing from.

The council asks that you are at least 21, with no upper age limit, and have a spare room for a child. You can be single, in a settled relationship, married or in a civil partnership, with or without children of your own, and you can keep working if your job is flexible enough for a child's needs. No qualifications are required, though experience with children helps. The assessment includes a DBS check, a medical and six personal references; offences against children or of a violent nature can rule someone out, but not every conviction does. Some households care for a child for a week or a year, others until adulthood, and part-time fostering is offered alongside full-time care.

Choosing the council means caring for the borough's own children with its supervising social workers behind you. It pays a fee and an allowance but does not publish the weekly amounts online, so ask for them. Its support list includes preparation courses and training, consultation meetings, an annual conference, training in managing behaviour and a therapist carers can turn to, and its flyer says a carer already approved elsewhere can transfer in as little as six weeks. Agencies set their own pay and support, so put the same questions to them.
Our Telford page covers the town itself, and the Shropshire, Wolverhampton and Staffordshire pages list services across the wider area.
